gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the BLUETTI Elite 100 mini's Power Lifting mode covers only resistive appliances up to 1,400 W while its product page caps total AC output at 700 W, so a 1,500 W kettle or heater sits above even the boosted limit.
standout_why: Compared against PopSci's Black Friday deals page (the cited one), OutletPicks' 1,000–1,299Wh page, Backup Power Hub, Solar Generator Prices and JuiceBench, all opened 2026-11-27. None explains Power Lifting, surge, compressor start-up or inverter idle draw. PopSci gives the Elite 100 mini only as 700 W continuous. OutletPicks carries 'Power Lifting 1400W' only in the BLUETTI image alt text, with no definition, so the figure is partly there already. Backup Power Hub uses an unexplained 0.85 runtime factor. I could not source the voltage-lowering mechanism itself in BLUETTI's own words, which keeps this at 1.
decides: It confirms the 1,500 W kettle/heater split and does not change the pick. The Elite 100 mini stays the light-load row: 700 W total, and its 1,400 W resistive-only boost is still under a 1,500 W nameplate. The page can state this more precisely than ChatGPT's 'rules out most kettles, heaters, and microwaves'. Whether the DJI Power 1000 V2 or Pecron E1000LFP holds its rated output down to empty is not settled here, because neither maker's pages would open.

findings.label: Total AC output cap (maker's footnote)
findings.value: 700 W total: "Total output not to exceed 700W. Actual performance may vary by device combination."
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Elite 100 mini Portable Power Station |1,004Wh 700W
findings.note: The page text as fetched names what the 700 W is for: "portable fridges, Wi-Fi routers, TVs, fans, lights, laptops, phones". It carried no Power Lifting figure, no surge figure and no overload behaviour.

findings.label: Power Lifting mode limit and load type (BLUETTI launch release)
findings.value: 1,400 W, resistive appliances only: "Power Lifting Mode supports compatible resistive appliances up to 1,400W"; continuous AC output 700 W
findings.source_title: BLUETTI launches the Elite 100 mini, its smallest 1 kWh portable power for travel and home (iTWire, 'New product release', 4 Nov 2026)
findings.note: This is BLUETTI's announcement as republished by iTWire with no author named, not a BLUETTI-hosted page. Arithmetic: a 1,500 W kettle or space heater is 100 W over the 1,400 W lifting limit and 800 W over the 700 W rated output. The release names no specific appliances.

findings.label: UPS switchover
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Elite 100 mini Portable Power Station |1,004Wh 700W
findings.note: Maker's footnote: "Confirm power and UPS requirements of medical or highly sensitive equipment before use." The iTWire release says it "switches to battery power within 10ms of an outage".

findings.label: Weight, AC recharge, solar input, cycle life
findings.value: 23.6 lb; 80% in 90 minutes on 700 W AC; up to 350 W solar; 6,000+ cycles
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Elite 100 mini Portable Power Station |1,004Wh 700W
findings.note: Charging time is BLUETTI's lab figure ("laboratory testing under optimal conditions"). The iTWire release gives the cycle rating as "more than 6,000 cycles to 80% capacity". The page text gave no warranty length.

findings.label: Price, BLUETTI US store
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Elite 100 mini Portable Power Station |1,004Wh 700W
findings.note: Read with storecheck.py (search and product) and again on the page. Single variant 'Elite 100 mini'. No pre-order notice on the unit; the page lists 2–5 business days delivery.

findings.label: What the rival pages give for runtime and output mechanism
findings.value: Backup Power Hub: "Runtime (hours) ≈ capacity (Wh) × 0.85 ÷ load (W)", with no statement of what the 0.85 is; PopSci: "capacity in watt-hours tells you how long it runs"
findings.source_title: Black Friday Power Station & Solar Generator Deals 2026 (Backup Power Hub)
findings.note: PopSci quote is from https://www.popsci.com/gear/black-friday-portable-power-station-deals/, read the same day. Neither page, nor OutletPicks, Solar Generator Prices or JuiceBench, mentions Power Lifting, surge, compressor start-up or idle draw in body text.
